title: Empirical Bayes Rebiasing
claim: Naive biased estimates undercover and full debiasing inflates variance; learning the bias distribution and partially restoring bias gives shorter calibrated intervals.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, colored arrows linking panels, interval formulas in bottom boxes
description: Three side-by-side panels, titled (a) Biased in orange, (b) Debiased in blue and (c) Rebiased (ours) in red. Each has a dashed colored box at the top giving the statistical model: biased estimate, bias estimator, and the learned bias distribution G-hat with a small pink bell curve. Colored arrows run down into each panel and across between panels. Each panel shows three stacked number lines (tasks 1, 2 and n, with dots between them). Black ticks mark the true theta, and markers carry horizontal interval bars: an orange circle, a blue diamond, a red star. Gray arrows show the bias shifts. The interval bars shrink from wide blue to shorter red. Bottom boxes give the interval formulas, annotated 'risk miscoverage' and 'wider interval'. The eye goes first to the colored panel titles and arrows.
caption: From biased to debiased to rebiased. Vertical black ticks mark the true $\theta_i$. (a) Across $n$ parallel tasks, each biased estimator \smash{$\biased_i$} is offset from its target $\theta_i$ by a draw $b_i\sim G$; the small variance $\sigma_i^2$ makes \smash{$\biased_i$}\vadjust{\kern1.3pt} precise, but the resulting interval may undercover. (b) Subtracting an unbiased but noisy estimator \smash{$\hat b_i$} centers the estimator at $\theta_i$ but each individual \smash{$\debiased_i$} is itself noisy, with a wider confidence interval. (c) Empirical Bayes rebiasing estimates the task-level bias distribution \smash{$\widehat G$} from \smash{$\hat b_1,\ldots,\hat b_n$} (shown here as $\widehat G=\mathrm{N}(0,\widehat A)$ for illustration) and uses its posterior mean to partially undo the bias correction and yield a substantially shorter calibrated interval.
abstract: We study methods for simultaneous analysis of many noisy and biased estimates, each paired with an even noisier estimate of its own bias. The analyst's goal is to construct short calibrated intervals for each parameter. The standard debiasing approach, which subtracts the bias estimate from each biased estimate, inflates variance and yields long intervals. In this paper, we propose an empirical Bayes rebiasing strategy that starts from the fully debiased estimates and learns from data how much bias to reintroduce by estimating the unknown bias distribution. We provide convergence rates for the coverage of our intervals when the bias distribution is estimated using nonparametric maximum likelihood. Furthermore, we demonstrate substantial precision gains in prediction-powered inference, including pairwise LLM win-rate evaluations, as well as for inference of direct genetic effects in family-based GWAS.
